News.title: Labour’s bonfire on jobs must end – young Brits need careers, not costly schemes
News.content:
Labour’s bonfire of jobs must end

‘’JOBS! JOBS! JOBS!’’ should be the mantra of PM-to-be Andy Burnham.

The statistic of a million young people not in work or education shames this country. Welfare Secretary Pat McFadden knows this cannot go on.



He has been pushing for ways to achieve reforms without risking another backbench rebellion from lily-livered Labour MPs who sank Sir Keir Starmer’s bid to cut the benefits bill last year.

You can’t fault Mr McFadden for trying. But the compromise ministers have come up with, the Youth Jobs Grant, is classic Labour wrong-headed thinking.



Instead of a tax cut it offers a handout.

Businesses are bunged £3,000 to employ a youngster who has been out of work for six months.



Getting young people into work is vital, but taxpayers should not be paying employers to create jobs.

The £180million earmarked for this scheme would be better spent incentivising firms to employ more youngsters themselves.

How about rewarding bosses who take on Neets with a cut to their business and National Insurance rates?

That would show that boosting private enterprise creates jobs. Instead Labour’s only solution is to raise taxes on firms then throw good public cash after bad.



Starmer has seen unemployment and welfare surge on his watch.

Can we expect any better from Burnham? The man who has vowed to destroy the legacy of Margaret Thatcher should remember one thing: The Tories under Thatcher created more than a million jobs.

This Labour Government has put hundreds of thousands of those jobs on the bonfire.

Ed-ing for disaster

THE Government must listen closely to the verdict of its own cost of living czar.

Iceland boss Lord Richard Walker was commissioned in February to provide a detailed insight into how to help struggling families.



His conclusion is devastatingly clear.

“We cannot keep loading Net Zero policy costs onto household bills and then act surprised when families break under the weight,’’ he writes.

Lord Walker wants green levies and wider Net Zero costs taken off bills immediately. We couldn’t agree more.

It is obvious to everyone struggling to run a business or manage a family budget that Ed Miliband’s ruinous policies are unsustainable.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In any normal business, Ed would be out on his ear. But in the warped world of Whitehall, what are the prospects for this green-eyed zealout?



He’s in the running to be our next Chancellor.

News.title: Cost of caging teen killers soars towards £1,000 a night as bill now more than expensive than stays at The Savoy
News.content:
THE cost of caging teen killers has hit almost £1,000 a night, figures show — more than a stay at The Savoy hotel.

Taxpayers cough up £353,000 a year to house a single offender at Secure Children’s Homes.



They hold the most dangerous offenders aged ten to 17, who are too young for youth prisons.

Accommodation costs have risen 5.1 per cent in a year and are now £968 per night per person, Ministry of Justice figures show.



In contrast, a Queen Room at the five-star Savoy in London cost £790 last week, while a King Room was £945.

There are 13 of the homes across England and Wales, holding a total of 171 children.



Jon Venables and Robert Thompson — both ten when they murdered two-year-old James Bulger in 1993 — were initially held in such accommodation.

More recently, two 12-year-old boys who killed Shawn Seesahai with a machete in 2024 were sent to secure custody instead of a young offender institution.

Secure Children’s Homes are now the most expensive places in Britain’s criminal justice system.

William Yarwood, campaigns director at the TaxPayers’ Alliance, said: “Ministers must get these spiralling costs under control and ensure taxpayers are not paying luxury prices for a failing system.”



The Ministry of Justice said: “Children in custody are largely there for serious, often violent offences and have complex needs that require more support than most adult prisoners.”

News.title: Bonkers Bridget’s childcare plan is yet more punishment to taxpayers – why do decent folk always pick up the bill?
News.content:
THERE are days when many parents, even if they adore their young kids, long for a well-earned break.

The idea of not having to work but still being able to afford to lay in the park, read a book and relax on the grass is the stuff of dreams — especially in this weather.



And imagine knowing that while you are chilling out, your child is in nursery, happily playing with loving staff, while the mounting childcare bills are being picked up by someone else.

You’d think this is something that can only happen to the very rich — those lucky sods born with a silver spoon in their mouth and the bank of granny and grandad to provide for them.

But now, thanks to Labour’s childcare fairy Bridget Phillipson, this could soon become a reality for Britain’s unemployed benefit scroungers.



It sounds far-fetched, but our ridiculous Education Secretary sees it, somehow, as a good idea.

Those jobless layabouts who love a handout from Labour will definitely agree, too.

I don’t.

Bridget wants the Government’s offer of 30 free nursery hours a week for children aged nine months to four years, if both parents are in work, to be extended to jobless families.

I am not sure what planet this woman is on.



So that army of dossers who think an early morning meeting is a 10am appointment on the sofa with This Morning will be given yet another handout.

And once again, it’s the muggins taxpayers — hard workers like you and me — who will foot the bill.

Under Bridget’s plan, these people will get paid for doing absolutely nothing. Not even looking after their own kids.

The current childcare scheme in England is set to cost the taxpayer around £8billion a year by 2028. This universal childcare offer could see that soar to £15billion.

Why do parents need childcare if they are sitting at home?



Bonkers Bridget said: “There are families out there who can’t afford quality childcare because they aren’t working, and they struggle to work because they can’t afford quality childcare.

“So their children miss out on quality early years education. Where’s the sense in that?”

Bridget says her bright idea will ­support families who want to work.

In reality, it’s just going to make the laziest in society even lazier.

When people get a job then, yes, give them free childcare. Fair enough. It’s a great incentive.



But they don’t need it when they’re ­sitting at home.

The only plus side to Bridget’s barmy idea is that it could mean more kids get school-ready by going to nursery and learning a few life lessons.

Because, as the number of ­people claiming working-age ­benefits rises, so too has the number of kids rocking up to school in ­nappies and with no idea what a book or knife and fork are for.

I don’t believe these aren’t linked. The hard-working people in this country shouldn’t have to graft so there are more taxes in the kitty to bring up somebody else’s kids.

Why is it always the decent folk who pick up the bill?



This policy could boost our dwindling fertility rate for all the wrong reasons, too. Those who love a handout will pop out more kids, knowing they won’t have to look after them.

What a vicious, money- grabbing cycle.

If Labour wants to dish out money, how about rewarding the taxpayers? The ones working all hours to pay extortionate nursery fees, instead of giving more to the bone idle.

Or better yet, extend the childcare for those working parents to cover the school holidays instead.

Hard work is supposed to pay.



Under Labour, not working pays even better.

TALKING of jobs, There’s a reason they say: “If you want something done properly, do it yourself.”

A phrase penniless lottery winner Kath Main should have listened to.

She asked her mother Fiona to go and buy their lotto ticket with the same numbers they’ve used for the past 20 years.



Then poor old Fiona had to trundle back to the newsagent to check it. When the machine didn’t give a winning beep, the ticket was put in the bin.

Now, despairing Kath has realised it was in fact a winner and is furious that her mum put the ticket in the bin.

Lesson learnt. When there’s £12million at stake, don’t delegate.

SORT IT OUT GIRLS

HOW tragic that, on the 30th anniversary of Wannabe, the Spice Girls can’t even put out a joint Instagram post because Mel B and Geri are at loggerheads.



These women got to where they are today because of the loyal fans who clung to their Girl Power message for decades.

Now they’re letting them down.

They should realise that life is short and listen back to the song that made them famous, which includes the line: “Friendship never ends.”

The greatest legacy of the Spice Girls was never just the music, it was the message.

Maybe, on this anniversary, they should remember that.



CHEERFUL CHARLES AND CAMILLA POPPIN TO ZOO

THEY may be the King and Queen, but seeing Charles and Camilla with the penguins at London Zoo this week reminded me of Dick Van Dyke and Julie Andrews, with a parasol above her head, in Mary Poppins.

If His Majesty had broken out into a dance, he really would have p-p-perked up those penguins.

PRICE OF LOVE



HOW sad that pensioner Anthony Eslick and his wife Pauline spent £25,000 on their poorly cat Millie to try to keep her alive after she fell ill three years ago.

Finally, when their life savings ran out, they had to put her to sleep.

I hope they realise they did all they could and can treasure their happy memories of that little black and white cat.

Ministers are considering introducing an independent regulator to help keep vet charges in check.

This really can’t come soon enough. Anthony and Pauline aren’t alone in their suffering.



Since 2015, when the big fat-cat vet companies swallowed up most of the smaller independent businesses in this country, prices have risen by 60 per cent.

That is disgusting. It’s ridiculous. It’s preying on people at the most desperate of times.

It is not just animal cruelty – it is owner cruelty, too.

MORAL OF THE STORY MY seven-year-old is your average kind of kid – the type who would sit glued to a tablet 24/7 if I left him to it. That was until I took him to see Toy Story 5 last Sunday. It’s all about a child who can’t make friends because none of the other children play with toys like hers, because they’re rude little gits who are glued to their electronic devices. What a life lesson this film was for my little boy. Please, go take your kids. Forget about the ridiculous price of the popcorn and get a front row seat. In the past six days, my son has played football, a bit of Uno and hasn’t asked to play his Sonic game on the tablet ONCE.

IT’S odd that a new study to find out is sniffing chocolate boosts gym performance only included men.

The 23 fellas in their 20s, who hadn’t eaten for ten hours, proved that the higher the cocoa content they sniffed, the more weightlifting leg extensions they did.



Seems a bit sexist not to include women. But then, thinking about it, who is the secret chocolate muncher in your house?

I know who it is in mine, and it isn’t The Geordie.

If they’d included women, they may have done more than sniff it.

TRACKED IT DOWN

AVANTI West Coast has often been a source of frustration for me and my fellow passengers.

Moans include how late the trains are, how slow they are, how dirty they are . . . you get the idea.



But this week I have nothing but good things to stay about their staff.

I left my old school diary/absolute life organiser on the train from Manchester to London and spiraled into a mild panic.

After a flurry of desperate calls and emails, a lovely train manager tracked it down.

I’ve never been so grateful to see a scruffy old diary.

On the way back, the train was 30 minutes late but hey, you can’t have everything in life, can you?



It gave me more time to plan my week ahead.

News.title: Prince Harry’s a rich thicko with a grudge – and I know the real victim of his ludicrous £50m legal fight with the Press
News.content:
AS Prince Harry’s war on the free Press ends in a crushing £50million legal defeat, this whining minor American celebrity should hang his balding head in shame.

The Duke of Sussex — how laughable that sounds — and his fellow celebrity claimants Elton John, Liz Hurley, Sadie Frost and the rest can no doubt afford to foot that £50million legal bill.



But why was Baroness Lawrence of Clarendon, the mother of the tragically murdered Stephen Lawrence, ever dragged into this ludicrous farce?

Because Prince Harry desperately wanted Doreen Lawrence by his side in his war against Britain’s free Press.

Harry recruited Doreen for his ­campaign. Harry sent her a text message telling her he had uncovered information she would want to know about relating to spying by the Daily Mail.



But it was not true.

A devastating 436-page judgment in the High Court by Mr Justice Nicklin crushed every last one of the lurid allegations that Associated Newspapers had spied on the claimants.

And every one of those damning 436 pages had Baroness Lawrence’s name — not Harry’s, not Elton’s — at the very top.

Without having Doreen Lawrence as Harry’s “trophy claimant”, this would have been a spat between rich celebrities and national newspapers.

You were used, Doreen.



This was never your fight.

And you are the real victim of this spectacularly botched legal action.

After an 11-week trial costing £50million, and after years when 40 hard- working, honourable journalists had false accusations of criminality hanging over their lives, Harry and his celebrity chums have been sent packing in the most emphatic way imaginable.

Yet Harry is STILL hiding behind Doreen Lawrence.

After the devastating verdict, the Prince and Baroness Lawrence issued a graceless “joint statement” calling the High Court’s decision “a complete and obvious whitewash.”



Is Prince Harry so steeped in self-pity and entitlement that he can’t see the stress that HE has imposed on Doreen Lawrence by dragging her into his crusade to kill the free Press?

I have met Doreen Lawrence.

She would have preferred to live her life far away from the spotlight.

Tragically, the racist murder of her 18-year-old son Stephen by racist thugs on April 22, 1993, changed the course of her destiny.

Doreen has fought racism. She has fought for justice for her murdered son.



And the bitter irony is that Doreen Lawrence never had a greater ally than the newspaper that Harry goaded her to sue.

The Daily Mail became synonymous with the Stephen Lawrence case in 1997 when it ran a front-page naming five men as Stephen’s murderers — and challenged them to sue for libel.

This was our free Press at its best.

But Harry and his celebrity chums want nothing more than to see every national newspaper journalist out of a job.

Harry is a rich thicko with a grudge.



And it would be comical to see him scuttling back to California with his ­miserable ginger tail between his legs if it were not for the hurt, distress and misery he has dumped on Doreen Lawrence.

Using this proud, decent woman as a front for his misguided mission was cynical beyond belief.

Reports suggest that the rich celebrity claimants will have a whip-round to pay those £50million legal fees.

Does that pampered prat, the Duke of Montecito, REALLY think that is the only debt to be paid?

Because I suggest you owe Baroness Doreen Lawrence an apology, Harry.



ALL THE BEST TO BRUCE

SAD news indeed that Bruce Foxton, formerly of The Jam, has been diagnosed with Parkinson’s Disease.

The Jam were one of the great British bands – three music-mad schoolmates who took their group all the way from Sheerwater Secondary School in Woking to Top Of The Pops.

The Jam were Paul Weller’s vision but all my memories of seeing the band have Bruce Foxton playing a co-starring role.

To see Paul and bassist Bruce flying through the air in their sweat-soaked suits and ties was to witness one of the greatest sights in British music – ever.



I remember the three of them being driven around in a van by John Weller, Paul’s dad.

I remember their fist fights (with each other).

And watching them at The Roxy when there were just four people in the audience – me and three members of The Clash.

Magical times.

And it would not have happened without the fire and skill of Bruce Foxton.



So all the very best, Bruce.

In what must be difficult days for you and your family, your many friends are thinking of you, and will forever hold you in our hearts.

ANDY’S BIN SO LUCKY…

LABOUR never really wanted Andy Burnham as their leader. The comrades went for Ed Miliband instead of Andy in the Labour leadership election in 2010, and poll-booth poison Jeremy Corbyn above Burnham in 2015.

It has taken Keir Starmer to make Burnham look like a good bet.



Burnham will soon be our unelected Prime Minister. Who voted for him?

A few hundred Labour drones worried about their jobs.

Where’s his mandate? He hasn’t got one.

What Andy does have is LUCK.

It is fortunate for Burnham that the man who has topped all opinion polls for three years is suddenly looking desperate.



Calling a snap by-election in Clacton is a rotten career move for Nigel Farage. It will not make any awkward questions about money go away. It is more likely to amplify them.

But at least the Clacton by-election gives us a chance to properly scrutinise the manifesto promises of Count Binface, who pledges to build “one affordable house.” Which is a lot more believable than Labour’s vacuous vow to build 1.5million homes within five years.

Lucky little Andy Burnham!

The Right are falling to bits just as the Left are getting their high-taxing, big-spending act together.

Andy will never be as popular as he will be in the coming months.



So just watch him call a snap General Election.

He may even win it.

Do we really need five more years of national self-harm from Labour?

That would be crazier than Count Binface.

FAREWELL TO A BONNIE LASS



BONNIE TYLER, who has died far too soon at the age of 75, was not just the grand master of the Eighties power ballad.

Bonnie was a tough, working-class coal miner’s daughter from the Welsh valleys.

Promoting her greatest hit, the multi-million selling Total Eclipse Of The Heart, a dumb Danish journalist had the temerity to yank her hair and ask her if it was real.

“I was so angry, I grabbed him by the balls and said, ‘Are they?’” Bonnie recalled. America loved her madly in the Eighties, when every song she sang sounded like it came from a Tom Cruise movie.

But at heart she was a Welsh blues belter.



Bonnie was called “the female Rod Stewart”, after surgery to scrape nodules from her vocal cords left her with that husky voice. A down-to-earth Janis Joplin – Bonnie’s hero – is much more like it.

Big hair, big songs. But the biggest thing about Bonnie Tyler was her heart.

IT should not be impossible for this country to send Rochdale rape gang leader Shabir Ahmed back to Pakistan.

It should not even be difficult. Pakistan are reluctant to take this pond scum back. It should not matter.

And it should not take leaving the European Convention on Human Rights or amending the 1971 Immigration Act for us to have the power to kick the bastard out.



In the last financial year, the UK sent over £100MILLION in aid to Pakistan – a country rich enough to afford its own nuclear weapons.

And if Pakistan will not take back Shabir Ahmed – and all the other rape gang members of Pakistani descent – then we should simply STOP SENDING £100MILLION IN AID TO PAKISTAN EVERY YEAR.

If Pakistan will not take back Shabir Ahmed, then stop all the lovely free money from the UK.

Then watch how quickly Islamabad changes its tune.

AIRHEAD Australian PM Anthony Albanese has sparked outrage Down Under by declaring that he would “shag” Kylie Minogue.



Comedian Nikki Osborne asked him, “Shag, marry, date – Kylie Minogue, Nicole Kidman or Rhonda Burchmore?”

The right answer was – why the hell am I being interviewed by a comedian? Shag, marry, date? More like grovel, apologise, resign.

News.title: Britain’s welfare safety net has become an easy payday – and it’s hardworking taxpayers picking up the tab
News.content:
WELFARE spending is out of control. If we are not careful, it will ­bankrupt Britain.

Under Labour, every taxpayer will be coughing up £5,000 a year for working-age welfare benefits by the end of this Parliament.



The fastest-growing part of the bill is a benefit called Personal Independence Payments or PIP. We now spend as much on this one benefit as we do on the entire policing budget.

The Government should be getting this under control. But they are not.



Last year, after Labour MPs rebelled and forced Keir Starmer into a humiliating welfare climbdown, a review was launched, chaired by welfare ­minister Stephen Timms.

His review reported back this week.



So, after months of waiting, what did it tell us? That the system is broken.

We already knew that.

People want the Government to fix things. Instead, the report just sets out lots of problems — including that they think benefits are too hard to get and should be more generous.

The welfare minister even said this week that benefits spending is “not of great concern”.



Labour are simply out of touch.

More than four million working-age people now claim sickness benefits.

Nearly half a million are under 25.

The number claiming PIP has doubled since the pandemic.

Britain hasn’t suddenly become twice as sick.



One in four people now class themselves as disabled.

Almost 40 per cent of PIP claims are for mental health ­conditions. More than 100,000 people now claim PIP for ADHD. That’s around 40 new claims every day under Keir Starmer.

Benefit fraud has topped £10billion for the first time. Labour has looked at all this, seen PIP spending heading towards £44billion by the end of the decade, and decided the answer is . . . more benefits.

It’s no wonder working people ask, “Why do I bother?” A family with three children in outer London, with both parents claiming PIP and Universal Credit health benefits, can receive more than £60,000 a year.



You would need to earn over £70,000 before tax to take home the same amount through work.

Taxpayers are also paying for Motability cars worth up to £40,000.

Blue Badges are being abused. Reports say British tourists are using PIP awards to jump the queues at Disneyland Paris.

Then there are the stories of people exaggerating or inventing illnesses to cash in. No wonder people are losing faith.



Exploding benefits bill

Britain has always believed in looking after those who genuinely need help.

We are a decent people.

What people won’t accept is paying for a system that pays out to those who could work but don’t, while asking those who do work to pick up the bill.

Our welfare state should be a safety net, not an easy payday.



Labour is also making benefit checks less frequent. There are thousands of claims for conditions including alcohol misuse and dyslexia, some even for headaches and acne.

Nobody wants to force someone who is terminally ill to go through unnecessary assessments, but there are lots of other conditions which could — and should – be reassessed regularly.

Instead, some claimants won’t be ­reassessed for four years or more, with these extensions meaning £20billion more in unchecked cash handouts.

Britain faces a £15billion hole in defence spending. Even Labour’s Tony Blair and ex-Defence Secretary Lord Robertson have argued that getting welfare under ­control is part of paying for our security.

Instead this Labour government is choosing a runaway benefits bill over our Armed Forces. Keir Starmer ­promised to put defence first and not hammer working people with higher taxes. He broke that promise.



But it’s not just Starmer. The problem is the Labour Party.

The Welfare Secretary Pat McFadden’s ­messages with Peter Mandelson revealed meetings with Labour MPs which were ­dominated by one question: Who can we tax to pay for more ­benefits?

Next week Andy Burnham inherits this mess. His in-tray will contain a ­crisis he can’t ignore: The exploding ­benefits bill. If he is serious about ­economic growth and serious about defending Britain, he must get a grip.

The fastest way would be to adopt our plan. The Conservatives would restore face-to-face benefit assessments and stop people gaming the system over the phone.

We would stop sickness benefits for mild mental health and neuro- diversity claims like anxiety, low moods and ADHD — because people struggling with these would be better off in work.



The Greens, Lib Dems and SNP all want to spend more on benefits too.

Reform talks tough but they couldn’t even decide a position on the two-child benefit cap. And instead of focusing his efforts on the country’s problems, Nigel Farage is going to spend the summer arguing with a bin.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

These are serious times, needing ­serious leadership. Getting the benefits bill under control takes more than ­slogans. It takes the courage to make difficult decisions.

We will soon find out whether Andy Burnham has the courage to do what Keir Starmer never would.

News.title: Car ‘seen parking at Ann Widdecombe house five minutes before her murder’ as cops pinpoint half-hour she was attacked
News.content:
DETECTIVES hunting Ann Widdecombe’s killer have pinpointed the half-hour period in which they believe she was bludgeoned to death.

The 78-year-old politician and Strictly star was interviewed on TalkTV at 8am on Wednesday and was due to appear on Channel 5’s Matt Allwright show at 1pm.



Ms Widdecombe replied to a text from a producer at 12.19pm but failed to join a Zoom link sent to her at 12.48pm, sources said.

It is understood studio staff made several unsuccessful attempts to contact her, then tried again that night and the following morning.



Copies of the final WhatsApp exchanges were last night released by ITV News, which produces the Allwright programme.

They show the last message sent by Ms Widdecombe at 12.19pm said: “Received! Panic over!!”



At 12.55pm, the producer messaged: “Hi Ann is everything ok?”

Her body was found around 11.30am on Thursday, when a carer or domestic assistant went to her bungalow in Haytor, Devon.



Channel 5 star Dan Walker confirmed: “Ann was due to appear on 5 Daytime but stopped responding to messages and didn’t turn up for the show.

“The team contacted her agent to ask them to check in on her.

“This information has been passed to police as it’s part of the investigation.”



The former Tory MP, later Reform UK’s immigration and justice spokeswoman, had been due to talk about close friend Nigel Farage’s Clacton-on-Sea by-election and the inquiry into his finances.

Mr Farage revealed a car was seen being parked outside her home minutes before she died.

Though the make and model of the vehicle was apparently seen on camera, it is understood the number plate was not visible.

Visiting the Dartmoor bungalow, Mr Farage suggested she was the target of a planned attack.

He said: “One theory doing the rounds is that it was a burglary gone wrong. But a car went on to the drive at approximately 12.25-12.30 on Wednesday.



“So if you were a burglar, would you literally drive your car on to someone’s drive?

“From what I can see of it, from what I make out, this was premeditated murder.”

Sources said Ms Widdecombe’s body was found in the kitchen and that she died from severe blunt trauma to the head.

The carer called 999 for an ambulance crew, who in turn ­notified police at 11.40am.

However, police last night faced questions over when they first realised Ann had been murdered.



Their first public statement and appeal for information over her death was only released on Friday afternoon — after Sun Online broke the news that she was suspected to have been murdered.

It was in a new statement released yesterday that police said they “believe the attack took place on Wednesday at around 12.30pm”.

Meanwhile, a 26-year-old man arrested on Friday afternoon was released from custody, with cops saying he is no longer part of the investigation.



Last night Devon and Cornwall Police Assistant Chief Constable Matt Longman said they had made an “active decision” on operational grounds not to release descriptions of any suspects or CCTV images.

He added: “Releasing such ­information prematurely could ­compromise ongoing inquiries and may prejudice future investigative opportunities.”

Retired detective chief inspector Mick Neville told The Sun on Sunday this could signal police have a strong idea who the suspect is.

Mr Neville, who founded the Met’s ­central images unit, said: “In my experience the police only release CCTV if officers are unable to identify a suspect who has been caught on camera.

“Putting an image in the media may result in an identification but it also warns the suspect that police are actively looking for him and may result in evidence being lost.”



Officers carried out further forensic checks at the bungalow and extended the cordon around it.

Nearby moorland was searched and a dozen officers were seen raking undergrowth at the side of the single-track road leading to the house, named Widdecombe’s Rest.

Mr Longman said: “Our priority remains identifying those responsible and ensuring that all available evidence is thoroughly examined.

“Detectives continue to carry out numerous inquiries as part of the ongoing investigation and we remain committed to establishing the full circumstances surrounding the incident.”

He added: “We believe the attack took place on Wednesday at around 12.30pm. Our inquiries are moving at pace for a suspect who is believed to be a white male.”



He thanked people who have already come forward with information and said: “Officers are making progress and are pursuing a number of lines of inquiry.”

Mr Neville said: “The fact the police know they are dealing with a white male suspect suggests they have a CCTV image of him.

“The extraordinary thing here is that the police seem to have waited so long before going public with their belief she was murdered.



“Tributes from close friends and loved ones were being issued after Ann’s death but none of them seemed to have a clue that she was the victim of murder.

“No politicians or the Government were seemingly aware of it either.

“It suggests police may not have been initially sure about whether she was murdered until her body was examined by a pathologist and the fatal wounds were discovered.”

Mr Neville continued: “Murder squad detectives describe the first 24 hours as the golden period for finding clues and suspects. But in this instance it was more than 48 hours after Ann’s body was found that the police put out an appeal.

“In that time the suspect could have got rid of their clothing or even gone abroad.”



An impromptu memorial for Ms Widdecombe was yesterday set up opposite the Moorland Hotel, around half a mile from her home.

It included flowers left by Mr Farage, who bowed his head for a moment’s silence as a mark of respect before giving an impromptu tribute speech.

Mr Farage said he had spoken twice with the Devon and Cornwall chief constable James Vaughan about the case.

He said of the killer: “It could be an individual with a grudge. It could be somebody with serious problems.



“But what is certain to me is that you don’t arrive in the middle of a little country (lane) on the edge of Dartmoor, park on a drive and go into a house just before half past 12 in the middle of the day without the motive being there from the very start.

“I just personally think the idea of a burglary . . . it just makes no sense to me at all. No sense to me at all.”

The Reform leader said politics “is very much more dangerous than it’s ever been”.

Referring to the 1990 murder of BBC Crimewatch host Jill Dando outside her home in Fulham, he added: “Whatever the outcome of the motives of the killer, let’s just hope and pray, this is not a Jill Dando type case where they don’t find a person. I believe with modern technology they will.”



Mr ­Farage said of the killer: “There are no words that I can utter about somebody who’s committed this act of barbarity against an innocent 78-year-old lady who wouldn’t harm a fly.

“I just hope that the killer is caught as quickly as possible and brought to justice.” Police have consulted counter-terror cops about the case but terrorism has been ruled out as a motive, suggesting ­detectives do not believe that Ms Widdecombe’s death was politically motivated.

The initial suspicions that she was murdered by a burglar are being re-evaluated with police considering a number of different motives.

Meanwhile locals yesterday described their area as “very safe.”

Christine Maloney said it was not unusual for people to leave their cars and front doors unlocked.



She said of Ms Widdecombe: “My husband saw her a week ago, driving around. I’m very shocked at her death, it shouldn’t have happened, it’s horrific.”

Fellow villager Alison Gilbert said of the politician, who moved to the area in 2008: “She was a really nice woman and she had a great sense of humour.

“Everyone saw her as quite an opinionated politician.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But to us she was just a person in the community. It’s a lovely area – you talk to strangers.”

Additional reporting: Thomas Godfrey and Julia Atherley

News.title: Eerie pic of 4ft tall diamond-shaped UFO hovering 200ft over US nuclear plant released as gov ‘baffled’ by sightings
News.content:
A DECLASSIFIED government report has revealed a silent, diamond-shaped UFO hovered just 100 to 200 feet above America’s primary nuclear weapons plant.

The craft appeared to speed up and change direction when security officers tried to chase it down.



The object was picked up by Ground Surveillance Radar at the Pantex Plant near Amarillo, Texas, at approximately 7:10 am on September 1, 2015, according to a declassified report published on the Department of War’s UAP archive.

Security officers scrambled to follow the craft in vehicles as it drifted northward at 10 to 15 mph, but were unable to catch up to it.



When officers stopped and got out of their vehicle to observe it through binoculars, they noted the object made no sound and had no visible means of propulsion, according to the report.

Officers in a separate armored vehicle tracked the object for three to five minutes using a remote camera system, confirming it was flying 100 to 200 feet above the ground.

Read more on UFOs DARK DISCOVERY Sinister twist in riddle of missing space experts as scientist found dead

The craft was described as diamond-shaped, rounded at the top, roughly 4 feet tall and 2 feet wide at the base.

Witnesses disagreed on its color, with some saying it was black and others describing it as silver, red, and blue.



The object appeared to pick up speed and change direction as officers pursued it, heading northeast before disappearing near County Road G and FM 1342.

The Carson County Sheriff’s Office was called in to assist, but a deputy who responded to the area said he did not see the object.

The release came as the White House’s newly appointed UFO council chief Avi Loeb admitted the government is “baffled” by what it has been seeing.



Loeb was tapped in early June by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence to assemble a team of scientists to make sense of the government’s UFO sightings.

“The U.S. government had me at hello,” he told Fox News.

“The fact that they are reaching out to scientists like myself indicates, in my mind, that they are baffled by what they are seeing, and they think that maybe it’s not human-made.”

The village, in Almeria, is said to be home to around 70 percent of British inhabitants, most of whom are elderly and retired. Bedar is also a popular destination for Brit holidaymakers.

Several Brits are feared to have perished in the blaze, including four found dead in a burned out car and possibly more in a group of people found to have attempted to flee the flames on foot.

News.title: Trump 'leaves instructions' on what to do if Iran assassinates him after claiming '1,000 missiles loaded'
News.content:
Trump 'leaves instructions' on what to do if Iran assassinates him after claiming '1,000 missiles loaded'

The US earlier demanded that Iran publicly state the Strait of Hormuz is open and that ships using the vital waterway will not be attacked - but officials blamed the latest strikes against vessels on a power struggle in Tehran

View 2 Images Donald Trump has revealed he’s left his advisors “instructions” for if he’s assassinated by Iran (Image: Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Donald Trump has revealed he’s left his advisors “instructions” for if he’s assassinated by Iran.

‌



The US President made the bold statement after days of labelling himself Iran’s “No. 1 target”. He said: “I’ve left instructions — if anything happens, to just literally bomb them at levels that they’ve never seen before.”

‌



Trump’s warning came after open calls for his death at the funeral of Iran’s late supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Responding on his Truth Social channel, he wrote: “1000 Missiles are Locked and Loaded and aimed at the Islamic Republic of Iran, with thousands of more to immediately follow, should the Iranian Government act on its threat, pronounced in many corners of the Globe, to assassinate, or attempt to assassinate, the sitting President of the United States of America, in this case, ME!

‌



“The U.S. Military is ready, willing, and able, for a one year period of time, subject to extension, to completely decimate and destroy all areas of Iran - PRAISE BE TO ALLAH! President DONALD J. TRUMP.”

View 2 Images Donald Trump is not happy with New York Times journalist Maggie Haberman, and he made it known over at Truth Social (Image: Getty Images )

‌



Donald Trump health fears after he admits ANOTHER hospital visit just six weeks after last physical READ MORE :

The US earlier demanded that Iran publicly state the Strait of Hormuz is open and that ships using the vital waterway will not be attacked. Officials have blamed the latest strikes against vessels on a power struggle in Tehran with rogue hardliners trying to derail the fragile truce.

Trump previously said the US has agreed to continue talks with Iran following recent clashes but stressed the ceasefire was over. But just as Washington was seeking public guarantees over the strait, Tehran’s top diplomat insisted any activity in the Gulf channel “rests exclusively with Iran”.

Ending Tehran’s stranglehold on the sea route had been a key demand in previous negotiations. But the initial deal reached between the US and Iran only provides for safe, toll-free passage of the waterway for 60 days, pending the outcome of a final agreement on Tehran’s disputed nuclear plans.

Article continues below

The pact also leaves it to Iran and Oman, along with other Gulf states, to “define the future administration and maritime services in the Strait of Hormuz”. It comes as Iran has continued demanding ships seek permission to transit through the strait.

It’s not the first time Trump has indicated he wants the US military to destroy the country should Iranian officials follow through on alleged plans to assassinate him. While signing an executive order threatening “maximum pressure” against the regime in February 2025, the president said the country “would be obliterated” if he is killed.

News.title: Ann Widdecombe's final messages revealed in haunting exchange as she wrote 'panic over!' before death
News.content:
Ann Widdecombe's final messages revealed in haunting exchange as she wrote 'panic over!' before death

The former politician and Strictly Come Dancing alum was due to speak on ITV Channel 5's Matt Allwright show, and communicated with a producer moments before her death

View 6 Images Widdecombe was due to appear on ITV the day she died (Image: Ken McKay/ITV/Shutterstock)

Ann Widdecombe's final text exchange has been revealed, and she said "panic over!" in a message to television producers before she died last week.

Police are investigating whether the former Conservative, Brexit Party and Reform politician was murdered after she found dead at her home in Hayton Vale, Devon, on Thursday, nearly 24 hours after police believe she died at 12.30pm on Wednesday. She had been due to appear in a television interview that day, ITV revealed, around the time she was believed to have been attacked by an unknown assailant.

The network has released correspondence between a producer of Channel 5's Matt Allwright show - on which she was due to appear via Zoom - and the politician, who was asked: "Is everything ok Ann?" as she likely lay dead.

Ann Widdecombe murder probe: Haunting final messages revealed after major police update on CCTV READ MORE :

View 6 Images A man lays flowers outside the house of Ann Widdecombe in Haytor (Image: Getty Images)

ITV, which previously confirmed having been in communication with Widdecombe moments before her death, revealed her last text and the panicked response of a producer hoping to have her contribute to the Channel 5 show. The full text exchange published by the network shows that she had said "panic over!" just 12 minutes before she died.

The full text exchange

12.14pm: Researcher: Not yet. Looked a few seconds ago! (12:14)

12.15pm: Researcher: Hi they said they sent it to you, but maybe it’s to the wrong email address

12.15pm: Anne Widdecombe: We spoke. Sorry for the confusion. I can see now that what I refused today was extra time!! Old age is a terrible thing.

12.15pm: Researcher: Would you mind sending me the address you’d like to receive it from

12.15pm: Anne Widdecombe: We spoke. Sorry for the confusion. I can see now that what I refused today was extra time!! Old age is a terrible thing.

View 6 Images Police in Haytor Vale, Devon outside the home of Anne Widdecombe where she was found dead (Image: Wayne Perry)

12.16pm: Researcher: Haha no problem!

12.16pm: Anne Widdecombe: It is the usual one that you always use. [email address blurred]

12.17pm: Researcher: That’s strange they did send it t[o] that address

12.17pm: Researcher: At 9:20 this morning

12.17pm: Researcher: I’ll send it to you now

12.18pm: Anne Widdecombe: It is the usual one that you always use [email address blurred]

12.18pm: Researcher: Just sent to this address, let me know if you’ve got it

View 6 Images Ann Widdecombe's last TV appearance was on TalkTV (Image: TalkTV/X)

12.19pm: Anne Widdecombe: Received! Panic over!!

12.19pm: Researcher: Amazing! Let me know if there’s any issues

‌



12:48pm Researcher: Hi Ann could you join the zoom now please

View 6 Images Widdecombe's neighbours said they had no idea why someone would want to hurt her (Image: Stuart Clarke/Shutterstock)

12.53pm: Voice call — No answer

‌



12.55pm: Researcher: Hi Ann is everything okay?

1.05pm: Voice call — No answer

1.14pm: Voice call — No answer

‌



Widdecombe's final televised appearance was on a TalkTV broadcast on Wednesday morning, during which she spoke about the upcoming Clacton by-election.

Devon and Cornwall Police have launched a manhunt for Widdecombe's possible killer after releasing a previous suspect, who was arrested on suspicion of murder, from police custody on Saturday morning. The service's Assistant Chief Constable, Matt Longman, said in an update this afternoon, however, that no further information would be issued regarding the investigation.

Pictures from the scene show a sizeable police contingent remains in the area around Widdecombe's house, both inside the property, around the Hayton community, and beyond, including the Dartmoor moors.

‌



View 6 Images Police on the road in Haytor Vale (Image: Wayne Perry)

Nigel Farage, who said he was expecting Widdecombe to help him campaign for his upcoming byelection in Clacton, made an appearance in the town today where he spoke about bringing her suspected killer to justice. He said: “Whatever the outcome of the motives of a killer, and let's just hope and pray, this is not a Jill Dando type case where they don't find a person.

“I believe with modern technology they will.” Asked for a message to the at-large killer, the Reform leader said: “There are no words that I can utter that somebody who's committed this act of barbarity against an innocent 78-year-old lady who wouldn't harm a fly.

Article continues below

“I just hope that the killer is caught as quickly as possible and brought to justice, that's all I can say.”
